newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP passes tv law at third reading.
newsitem.headline: EP passes tv law at third reading.

text.p: The European Parliament on Tuesday gave final approval to the revised television without frontiers directive, passing it unamended at third reading.
The revised version of the 1989 law -- 89/552/EEC -- the result of April's conciliation procedure -- is now expected to be adopted at the June 30 Culture Council meeting in Luxembourg.

The process of revising the law, which lasted more than two years, became as complex as some of the soap operas shown on television, as France and Euro-MPs fought vainly for stricter limits on the number of Hollywood films and sitcoms.
"Sadly we missed a great opportunity to create a level playing field in the audiovisual sector," British Socialist deputy Carole Tongue lamented in parliament.
"TV is Europe's Hollywood," she said dramatically. "It will help ensure that we create and view our own stories, be it Inspector Morse or Derrick."
The parliament was able to secure rules forcing member states to respect each others' lists of major sporting events which must be shown free.
